betterCitation: Ibn Khaldun, The Muqaddimah, Book One, the opening discussion on untruth in history (trans. Franz Rosenthal, 1958)
reason: Refuted on the locator, not on the words. The wording is Rosenthal's, character for character, and I read it in two independent copies of his translation rather than in a quotation site. First I downloaded the very page the verifier cited, the oceanlibrary chunk, and pulled the raw markup: the sentence stands at byte 3666 of the file, it reads Untruth naturally afflicts historical information. There are various reasons that make this unavoidable. One of them is partisanship for opinions and schools, and the nearest heading above it in the HTML is Book One of the Kitab al-Ibar. Then I fetched a second, unrelated scan of the same Rosenthal translation as a PDF and extracted its text, where the sentence occurs exactly once in 12,786 lines of the whole work, at line 62, again directly under the Book One title and its descriptive subtitle about the nature of civilization. So the card's section, the Introduction, is the wrong one. Rosenthal's own table of contents, printed three times in the front of that PDF, keeps the two apart in so many words: Introductory material, INVOCATION FOREWORD INTRODUCTION, and then separately Introductory material of Book One, Kitab al Ibar. The two openings are different sentences and I have both. The INTRODUCTION begins at line 1068 with IT SHOULD BE KNOWN that history is a discipline that has a great number of approaches, under the heading The excellence of historiography, an appreciation of the various approaches to history, a glimpse at the different kinds of errors to which historians are liable, something about why these errors occur. Book One begins with IT SHOULD be known that history, in matter of fact, is information about human social organization, and the seven reasons for untruth, partisanship, reliance upon transmitters, unawareness of the purpose of an event, unfounded assumption, ignorance of how conditions conform with reality, the wish to flatter the great, and ignorance of the nature of civilization, follow there and nowhere else. I can see exactly how the verifier was caught: its locator phrase, the discussion of the errors to which historians are liable and why they occur, is a near quotation of the INTRODUCTION'S OWN TITLE, and that title does describe a discussion of historians' errors, with the al-Masudi and Israelite army examples under it. But the famous sentence is not in that section. A reader sent to the Introduction of the Muqaddimah will not find it, which is precisely the harm a section-level locator is supposed to prevent, and the harm is larger here because the work's own common subtitle is An Introduction to History, so the word Introduction on the card reads as a section and points at the wrong one. Everything else about the line holds and I could not break any of it. Attribution is Ibn Khaldun's own prose, not reported, not a character, so no speaker is owed; the misattribution list carries no Ibn Khaldun trap. shipped.js returns no shipped hit, no near-hit, zero lines for the year, not banned, not at cap, and no Ibn Khaldun appears in carry.json or anywhere else in June. Scope is clean: fourteenth century, philosophy of history, not scripture, not oratory, publishable, and on the theme of truth and clarity at its plainest. The translator and the year of the translation are named as rule 4 requires, and Bollingen Series XLIII, Pantheon, 1958 is the right edition for that wording. The source line leads with the name, carries no dash, no straight double quote, and runs 118 characters. The fix is one phrase, and the better citation above is 114 characters.

residual: Only the page range. The reference site's volume 1, pages 35 to 36 does not match what I read: the Book One text carries a footnote pointing to p. 76 below, which puts the passage nearer p. 71 of Rosenthal's first volume. The verifier was right to keep the card at section level rather than print that page range; it just named the wrong section.
